newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher on U.S. Treasuries gains.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher on U.S. Treasuries gains.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose late Thursday, putting in a strong performance on the back of large gains by U.S. Treasuries after subdued producer prices.

"There was a bit of buying by everybody," said a trader at a foreign bank. Activity started slowly but picked up gradually during the session. Argentine Brady bonds put in the strongest performance, benefitting the most from the U.S. Treasury gains.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.25 to 123.90 while Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 5/8 to 86-7/8.

The strongest local performing bond was the peso-denominated Bocon Previsional 1 due 2001, which gained 0.80 pesos to 119.40. Traders said that bond gained as the recent gains had made investors more adverse to the larger risks of investing in peso paper.

"The news from Argentina is good," said another trader, pointing to the total $3.0 billion worth of global bonds the government announced earlier in the week it will issue before April. The more debt Argentina can issue before October's Congressional elections the better, say traders.
Call money rates fell to 5.48 percent from 5.63 percent.
